messages:
luis_customer: Hey team, we're seeing a big jump in p95/p99 latency for our tool-calling flows since ~04:00 UTC. Users hit timeouts and we get 504s. Sample request-id: req_9f3a2b. Payloads are large nested JSON with multiple tool calls in sequence.

alex_support: thanks for reporting — can you paste a minimal repro and the timestamped request-id? Also roughly how many tool calls per request?

luis_customer: repro attached (sanitized). Sequence has 3 tool calls: geocode -> enrich -> execute. Typical payload ~120KB. curl: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-xl", "input":{...}, "tools":["geo","enrich","exec"], "call_mode":"sequential"}'
```

luis_customer: request-id in logs: req_9f3a2b, happened at 2026-03-14T04:12:33Z. p95 went from ~200ms to ~1.8s, p99 to ~3.2s for this tenant. Other tenants slightly impacted.

alex_support: copying in @maria (SRE) and @jamie (runtime) to triage. I'm flagging severity-3 since user-facing errors but not whole service down.

maria_sre: looking at cluster metrics now. I see a spike in the tool-router latency histogram around 04:10 UTC that aligns with this request-id. Router CPU also up ~30% on the routing pod pool. Any idea if schema validation was enabled for this customer?

jamie_runtime: we rolled a minor router change yesterday (router v2.6.1) that added strict JSON schema validation for tool outputs. It runs validation synchronously before forwarding to the next tool. That could add linear overhead with nested outputs. I pushed a quick flamegraph for the router: ```[router] top frames: validate_json_schema 35% -> route_to_tool 25% -> encode_response 15% -> network_send 10%```

noah_ml: tool outputs for that tenant are pretty nested; validation cost grows with object size. Also the router does a deep clone for each tool hop which doubles memory/copy overhead.

maria_sre: OK that matches. If validation is O(n) on payload size and we have 3 calls sequentially, latency multiplies. For p99 it's crushing some nodes. Immediate mitigation options: 1) disable strict validation via feature-flag for affected customers, 2) route heavy-tool flows to the legacy router (no deep-validate), 3) enable streaming passthrough (skip validation but stream responses). Thoughts?

jamie_runtime: quick mitigation: flip `router.strict_tool_schema` to false for the tenant group. That should remove the validation step. I can do a scoped feature-flag change in the console. Also we can add a short-term bypass to avoid deep clone: set `router.copy_mode=shallow` (risky but temporary).

alex_support: Luis — would turning off strict validation be acceptable for you while we investigate? It relaxes JSON schema enforcement for tool outputs.

luis_customer: yes please flip it for our org id org_44. We prefer availability. Keep us posted about data safety implications.

maria_sre: I'll schedule the change: target at 04:30 UTC. Also creating a canary rollout to 10% of traffic first. We'll monitor p95/p99 and CPU. If stable, roll to 100% in 10m.

jamie_runtime: done: applied feature-flag `router.strict_tool_schema=false` scoped to org_44 at 04:31:12Z. Canary: 10% of org_44. Logging now shows validate_json_schema falling out of hot path for those requests.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: feature-flag change by jamie_runtime (ID ff-2026-0314-09). Canary started at 04:31:12Z.

maria_sre: after canary p95 dropped from 1.8s to ~240ms for canaryed requests; CPU normalized. p99 improved but still slightly high — looks like deep-clone overhead still present for some flows. We'll wait full rollout.

jamie_runtime: follow-up: we should implement async validation as the proper fix. Sketch: validate in background, if it fails mark trace and issue a rollback for that tool invocation instead of blocking. That avoids tail latencies. Also adding streaming JSON validation (chunked) would lower peak mem.

noah_ml: agree — async validation + schema-level sampling (validate 1% of calls) to catch regressions without adding latency. We'll also add a metric `schema_validation_duration_ms` tagged by payload_size.

alex_support: Action items: - jamie: implement feature-flaged async validation RFC + timeline (ETA 2 weeks). - noah: add sampling and metric. - maria: run post-mortem and recommend durable mitigation (router copy elimination). - luis: confirm customer acceptance of temporary flag.

luis_customer: confirmed, thanks. Can you send us a short SLA note about the change and whether any outputs might be malformed?

alex_support: will draft. For transparency: turning validation off temporarily means we won't block malformed tool outputs — best-effort pass-through. We will keep logs and issue alerts on validation failures once async sampling is live.

maria_sre: I'll keep this thread open and attach traces once full rollout completes. Closing note: if anyone sees regression after rollout at 04:40 UTC ping here. :thumbsup:
